updates.title: Monsoon season: plan for rain during exams
updates.body: MKN says the Northeast Monsoon started on 27 October and runs until March 2027. MetMalaysia expects 3 to 5 spells of heavy, continuous rain from November to January, mainly on the east coast of the Peninsula, western Sarawak and northern and eastern Sabah. That overlaps the SPM and STPM papers, so plan your route to the exam centre early, follow MetMalaysia warnings (myCuaca app), and tell your school straight away if floods stop you getting there.

updates.title: SPM English speaking test starts today
updates.body: The English Speaking Test (1119/3) runs from today, 2 November, to 5 November. The BM speaking test finished on 29 October, and STAM 2026 ends today. Bring your IC and printed Pernyataan Pendaftaran Peperiksaan; missing the speaking test counts as absent for that subject. Next: science practicals from 16 November, STPM Semester 3 from 17 November and SPM written papers from 23 November.

updates.title: Budget 2027: living allowance for Form Six students
updates.body: The government will give Form Six (STPM) students a living allowance at the same rate as matriculation students, expected to help about 90,000 students. Payment dates and conditions have not been announced yet, so watch for KPM's official notice.

updates.title: SPM 2026 starts on Monday with the BM speaking test
updates.body: Ujian Bertutur Bahasa Melayu (1103/3) runs from 26 to 29 October. The English speaking test follows on 2 to 5 November. Written papers start on 23 November.

updates.title: STPM Semester 3 starts on 17 November
updates.body: The first paper is Pengajian Am 3 (900/3) at 8.00 am. The last paper is on 26 November.

updates.title: STAM 2026 is under way
updates.body: 4,291 candidates are sitting STAM at 131 centres, from 12 October to 2 November.

updates.title: Flood season: exams still go ahead
updates.body: JKM Kelantan says it is preparing so that SPM and STPM candidates at schools used as flood relief centres are not disrupted. Candidates affected by floods should contact their school straight away.
